CAP says that during a network partition a replicated store must give up either availability or linearizability (every read seeing the latest completed write). PACELC extends it: else, when there is no partition, you trade latency against consistency.

Want the plain version?
Real version: pick CP and you serve quorum reads that fail during a split; pick AP and you accept eventual consistency.

Imagine three friends keeping one shopping list by text message. If the texts stop getting through, each friend either stops adding items or keeps adding and risks a mismatched list.

That's the plain version, want the high-school one?
The CAP theorem names consistency, availability and partition tolerance; you can have two of the three.
